title: Lord, Who's the Happy Man, That May
description: Lord, Who's the Happy Man, That May in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 347 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, who's the hap-py man, that may To thy blest courts re-pair, Not, stran-ger like, to vis-it them, But to in-hab-it there?

lines: Lord, who's the happy man, that may
'Tis he whose every thought and deed
Whose generous tongue disdains to speak
Who never did a slander forge,
Nor hearken to a false report,
Who to his plighted vows and trust
And though he promise to his loss,
The man who by this steady course
When earth's foundations shake, shall stand

licence: Public domain: Nahum Tate died in 1715; Nicholas Brady died in 1726.
credits: Words by Nahum Tate (1652–1715) and Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
